newsitem.title: USA: CKS forms Europe unit, buys Germany's Prisma.
newsitem.headline: CKS forms Europe unit, buys Germany's Prisma.

text.p: CKS Group Inc said it has reached a definitive agreement to acquire Germany's Prisma Holding GmbH in a deal valued at up to $16.5 million to establish its initial presence in the European market.

The high-flying Silicon Valley interactive advertising and marketing communications agency said it is making an initial payment in cash and stock of $6.5 million and providing up to $10 million in additional consideration in cash and stock based on Prisma's operating results through 1999.
This is the first major international move for CKS.

Mark Kvamme, chairman and chief executive of CKS Group, told Reuters in an interview that Prisma is an integrated firm with a similar approach to both traditional and new media, and is also known for pioneering interactive on-line campaigns.

"It's not new for companies like ours to go international," Kvamme said. "But the important component is we're finding the Internet is making the world smaller, but you still need the local presence."
"You need to have the experience in all these different media both locally and globally," the CKS executive said.

CKS Group, which completed its initial public offering in late 1995, has benefited from the market euphoria over prospects for Internet businesses. The company's stock, valued at $17 the time of its initial public offering, closed on Thursday at 27-3/8, off 1/8 on the session.

Prisma, which provides direct marketing, advertising, public relations and channel marketing services in Germany, Switzerland and Austria, shares customers such as Apple Computer Inc and Microsoft Corp with CKS.
"Prisma is probably the closest to what CKS represents in any other company I've ever met. They are doing some really killer stuff," Kvamme said.

"We really do look at communications in a holistic way and we instantly share the same culture," he said. "Almost half of our business is technology marketing and they're very big in technology marketing."
Both companies have also extended beyond the technology sphere, with Prisma's client base also including companies such as the airline Deutsche Lufthansa and Stern magazine.
Prisma currently is comprised of around 80 people.

Kvamme said CKS plans to continue to expand overseas, and in Europe would make Prisma's headquarters in Hamburg its initial base, while looking for partnerships that could take advantage of established client relationships.
"This is the beginning of our international (expansion). We're looking at the rest of Europe and we're looking at Asia," the CKS chief executive said.
"We're going to, until further notice, put CKS Europe headquarters in Hamburg and start looking at other satellite offices throughout the continent," he said.
